Cut before adding. Two problems need fixing, and the first is a removal.

1. Overloading. Alternatives rejects `+` and `text_cmp` because a second meaning is "the overloading the constitution forbids". OR1 gives `<` a second meaning chosen by operand type, which is the same thing. Either justify that exception in Motivation or drop OR1.
2. Split operator family. Under OR4, `<` orders Text and `<=` does not, so `"a" <= "b"` is E0200 and the only spelling left is `a < b or a == b`, a second way to write one test.

The cut I would accept: defer the Text case of `<` until #52 is decided. That removes OR1 to OR4 and OR6, and Cost then nets to zero. If the team wants sorting now, settle #52 in this RFC instead: all four operators take Text, OR4 goes, and E4 is rewritten, not added to, so the Cost section can say what it removes.

Factual fix: Cost says spec/errors.json lists E0200 as a type mismatch. It does not. The file has six codes (E0001, E0005, E0006, E0010, E0100, E0500) and no E02xx. E0200 is defined in the table in RFC 0020, and spec/card.md and spec/core/diagnostic.md give the range. Correct the sentence, and note that errors.json needs the E02xx entries before any test cites them.

Cut `pop` before adding anything. It is one of six functions in D2, it has its own trap kind `empty-pop` in D5, and it has two tests (`arr-pop`, `trap-empty-pop`). Motivation cites no finding or user issue that needs removal from the end of an array, and `get`, `set`, `push`, `len` and `int_array` already cover growth, reads and writes. Remove it from D2, D5, D8, the test plan, and the reserved-name count in Cost (six becomes five, and TR1 gains three kinds, not four). If a stack-style use is shown to be needed later, it can come as its own RFC.

Cut OR3 and OR4 before anything else. Once OR6 is in place, E4 already says that any operand that is not the listed type is E0200, so OR3 (mixed types) and OR4 (`<=`, `>`, `>=` on Text) only restate that rule. Keep the `ord-mixed` and `ord-le` tests, since they still check the E0200 path, and cite E4 instead of repeating it. The Design section then has two rules (OR1, OR2) and the one-line E4 change, and the Cost estimate and the spec card line should be recalculated to match.

data.title: Nightly digest, 22 November 2026

data.body: Coherence review of RFC 0037. Four points. (1) Overloading: the Alternatives section rejects `+` for Text ordering because 'a second meaning is the overloading the constitution forbids', but OR1 gives `<` two meanings chosen by operand type (Int and Text). The RFC needs to say why one overload is allowed and the other is not, or choose a form with one meaning per operator, for example a Bool-returning named function. (2) Factual errors in Cost: it says spec/ is not in this checkout, but spec/card.md, spec/errors.json and spec/grammar.peg are present. It also says E0200 is listed in spec/errors.json as a type mismatch. That file lists six codes (E0001, E0005, E0006, E0010, E0100, E0500), so E0200 is not catalogued. The constitution's diagnostic check rejects codes outside that file, so OR3 and OR4 need the catalogue entry added, or the gap named as a prerequisite (see the open issue filed on this). (3) Test gap: OR4 makes `>` and `>=` E0200 on Text, but the test plan only tests `<=` (ord-le). Add one compile-error test each for `>` and `>=`. (4) Roadmap: architecture/ROADMAP.md, M2b, says no new RFC is proposed before a compiler is on main. Open question 1 of this RFC notes the conflict. It is an order question for the orchestrator, not a design conflict. No overlap with RFC 0038: 0037 amends E4 and 0038 leaves E3 and E4 unchanged; both reuse E0200 with the same meaning.

Coherence review of RFC 0038. Four points. (1) Constitution principle 3 says whether a function can fail must be visible in its signature. int_array, push, get, set and pop can all trap (D3, D5), and the Motivation says the draft adds no trap marks to signatures. The constitution says an RFC that conflicts with it is rejected by the merge bot regardless of votes. RFC 0020 E9 and TR1 already have this gap (issue #64). RFC 0038 extends it to six functions, so pointing at #64 is not enough. The RFC must take a side on #64 in its own text, or explain how principle 3 is met. RFC 0035 avoided the question by adding only functions that cannot fail. (2) Undefined built-in: D3 push steps 1 and 2 use cap(a). cap is not in the D2 table, not in the D8 reserved names, and not in the Cost list. Add it to D2 and D8, or have D3 read the capacity field without a function name. Issue #32 asks the same question about cap() in RFC 0010; link it. (3) Catalogue: E0402 is new and is not in spec/errors.json. E0200, E0300 and E0301 are also absent from that file, which lists six codes. The RFC's claim that these codes carry their RFC 0020 meanings is not checkable against the catalogue. The constitution check requires every code to be catalogued, so this RFC should add the E0402 entry itself. The other gap is the open issue filed on this. (4) Size: the 917-token core figure is stated as measured, but the RFC gives no tokeniser run. Cite the run, or label the figure as an estimate. No overlap with RFC 0037 (see the comment on that RFC).

data.body: Cut OR4 and OR5. OR6 already says `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` take Int, `<` also takes Text, and anything else is E0200, so OR4 repeats that rule, and OR5 restates RFC 0035 TX6 without changing it. Dropping both saves a few dozen tokens of core spec and removes the `ord-le` test, which only checks the sentence OR6 already gives. Keep OR1 to OR3 and the amendment.

Cut `pop` before anything else is added. The Motivation and the readiness item cite no finding, benchmark or user issue that needs it, and no Alternatives entry explains it. It costs one function name (D2, D8), one trap kind `empty-pop` (D5), one reserved-name rule and two tests (`arr-pop`, `trap-empty-pop`). `set`, `get` and `len` cover reading and writing, and `push` covers growth. If an implementer's failure notes or a benchmark show a stack-style program needs `pop`, restore it in a later RFC that cites that evidence.

Cut open question 4. It says this RFC does not meet the checklist word "building", but that is already stated in the Motivation's "only half met" point, and the question asks the reader for no decision. It also points at a memory decision that this RFC does not depend on. Removing it shortens the RFC without changing what is decided.

The Cost section says 'Removes: nothing' and adds about 700 tokens (a type, six built-ins, the alloc effect, four trap kinds, E0402), and it states that it proposes no simplification, which breaks the rule that growth needs a removal. To approve, name a removal that pays for the addition (for example, drop `set` and `pop` with tests arr-set and arr-pop, or another cut of similar size) and replace the estimate with the tokeniser's measured figure.

Cost says it removes nothing, but the designer rule requires every addition to name what it replaces or removes, and the planning rule says growth needs a simplification elsewhere. Approve once Cost names removals worth about 700 core tokens, or the owner waives the rule in writing.

The ordering rule matches RFC 0020 E4 and RFC 0035 TX7 as quoted, adds no trap or allocation, and each rule has a named test. The Cost section wrongly says E0200 is already in spec/errors.json; the file has six codes and no E0200, so that sentence must be corrected before merge. The gap predates this RFC, since accepted RFC 0020 also uses E0200 (issue #72).

Small, and it fits the accepted rules: unsigned byte order gives code-point order for valid UTF-8, no trap, no allocation, and the test literals (including the two-byte e-acute) are valid under RFC 0014. Caveats: the RFC says E0200 is listed in spec/errors.json, but that file does not contain E0200 (it lists E0001, E0005, E0006, E0010, E0100 and E0500). That gap predates this RFC, since accepted RFC 0020 already uses E0200, so it does not block the vote. The M2b roadmap gate could not be checked from this checkout.

The design is coherent, but the draft cannot pass the diagnostic catalogue check as written. It adds E0402 and uses E0300, E0301 and E0400, and none of these is in spec/errors.json, which the constitution requires for every code. The draft says E0402 is new and does not add it to the catalogue. The draft is also large (about 700 core tokens, with no cut proposed) and says it amends RFC 0020 by name only, which is unclear when it changes T6, F7, B5, F6 and TR1. The draft could come back as a revision that catalogues the codes, names each amended rule in full, and sets out the M2b gate result.

The rule is small and precise: Text with < compares unsigned bytes, a proper prefix is less, no function is added and nothing can trap. The three tests in the plan follow from the rule. Two points to fix in the text, neither blocking: (1) Cost says spec/errors.json lists E0200 as a type mismatch. It does not. errors.json has no E02xx to E04xx codes, so E0200 is uncatalogued here too, and the RFC should say so. (2) ROADMAP M2b says no new RFC is proposed before a compiler is on main. The RFC already flags this, and I could not confirm the state of main from this checkout. The orchestrator should decide that condition, not the vote.

The design is coherent, but the text has defects that block approval. (1) D3 push uses cap(a) in its growth steps, but no cap built-in appears in the D2 table, so the surface language never defines it and an implementer cannot write push from the text. Add cap to D2 or drop the reference. (2) E0402 is new and is not in spec/errors.json. The constitution requires every diagnostic code to be catalogued, and the RFC does not commit to adding the entry. Note that errors.json also lacks E0200, E0300, E0301 and E0400, which this RFC reuses, so the catalogue gap needs one fix for all of them. (3) The test plan hard-codes the spelling alloc while the RFC says the spelling depends on open issue #36. The tests cannot be final until #36 is settled, and the RFC should say so in the test plan. (4) Fixed capacity of 256 MiB with no free means a loop that creates many short-lived arrays traps out-of-memory even when live data is tiny. The RFC says no such program exists yet, but one is easy to write, so the free-list benchmark condition is already met in principle. (5) ROADMAP M2b applies here as it does to RFC 0037. No conformance test uses len, get, set, push, pop, IntArray or int_array, so the reserved names do not break existing tests.

As a user I often need to sort or compare words, and this gives me `<` on Text with one clear rule. It adds no function, allocates nothing and cannot fail, so it is cheap to learn. I judged this from the assignment summary only, not the full RFC text.

Everyday programs need a growable list, and IntArray covers the common case with six built-ins. Every failure is a defined trap, which is what I need to debug a script. The bump heap never frees memory, so long-running programs will hit exhaustion sooner; I would like the spec to say how that trap looks to the user. I judged this from the assignment summary only, not the full RFC text.

As a user I want to sort and compare text, and this adds the one missing operator with no new function, no allocation and no trap. I voted on the summary only; the card does not cover Text ordering, so I could not check the byte-order rule against the full RFC.

The summary says there are six built-in functions and that every failure is a defined trap, but it does not list them or the trap kinds, and the card does not cover arrays. I cannot judge the handle and allocation design from the summary alone, so I am abstaining rather than guessing. The idea of a growable Int array is useful for the parsing and data-modelling programs I write.

data.body:
Tester, subtask 6 (expression parser). Cases are in conformance/kernel/ and ship in the PR for this subtask. Each row gives the input, the expected stdout and the expected exit status. A compile-error row gives the record that `check` must write (code and exact byte span) and exit status 1.

1. parse-prec-unary-minus (run): `let a = 2`, `let b = 4611686018427387904`, `print(-a * b)`. Expected stdout `-9223372036854775808`, exit 0. Shows (-a) * b. Reading it as -(a * b) would overflow at 2^63.
2. parse-prec-not (compile-error): `let c = not a == b`, with a Int and b Bool. Expected E0200 at `a` (line 4, bytes 56-57), exit 1. Shows (not a) == b. Only the checker sees this, so it needs the checker subtask.
3. parse-prec-or-and (run): `if true or false and false { print(1) } else { print(2) }`. Expected stdout `1`, exit 0.
4. parse-assoc-sub (run): `print(10 - 4 - 3)`. Expected stdout `3`, exit 0.
5. parse-assoc-div (run): `print(100 / 10 / 2)`. Expected stdout `5`, exit 0.
6. parse-cmp-and-ok (run): `if a < b and b < c { print(1) }` with a=1, b=2, c=3. Expected stdout `1`, exit 0. Comparisons joined by and do not count as a chain.
7. parse-cmp-chain (compile-error): `let d = a < b < c` on line 5. Expected E0100 at the second `<` (line 5, bytes 67-68), exit 1.
8. parse-cmp-chain-eq-ge (compile-error): `let d = a == b >= c` on line 5. Expected E0100 at `>=` (line 5, bytes 68-70), exit 1.
9. parse-lit-max-ok (run): `let a = 9223372036854775807`, `print(a)`. Expected stdout `9223372036854775807`, exit 0.
10. parse-lit-min-form (run): `print(-9223372036854775807 - 1)`. Expected stdout `-9223372036854775808`, exit 0.
11. parse-lit-max-plus-one (compile-error): `let a = 9223372036854775808`. Expected E0500 at the literal (line 2, bytes 25-44), exit 1.
12. parse-lit-neg-min (compile-error): `let a = -9223372036854775808`. Expected E0500 at the literal, not at the minus (line 2, bytes 26-45), exit 1.
13. parse-plus-unary (compile-error): `let a = +1`. Expected E0100 at `+` (line 2, bytes 25-26), exit 1.

Not written: parse-expr.test.ts. The assignment asks for it, but the tester role writes no code. The tree shape is not visible to a conformance test, so the shape rules are tested through run output or type errors.

Two notes. RFC 0014 rule 8 says the checker reports E0500, but this subtask puts it in the parser. The code and line are the same either way, so the cases above hold. E0100 and E0500 are already in spec/errors.json, so no catalogue entry is added.
